## TL;DR

The live-update path mostly recovers on its own, but two things did not. A board refresh that failed right after a reconnect was never retried, so on a quiet repo the Control counts stayed at their pre-outage values until some unrelated frame arrived. And the header pill said "offline", hid its words below 720 px, and was not a plain-English reconnecting state. I fixed the retry, made a board that loads clear a stale offline banner, changed the copy to "reconnecting", and kept the word visible on phones. Browser checks at 375, 768 and 1280 px pass against fixtures and a simulated outage. The same browser test fails on the original store, so it is a real regression check.

## Work and rationale

The existing code already had jittered SSE backoff (#1018), a refresh on every open, and offline-banner clearing on stream frames (#1226). I read those paths before changing anything, then wrote the failing tests first so I could see the real gap.

The stale-data bug is in `connectSSE`. `onopen` calls `refresh()` and attaches `.catch(() => {})`. Frames emitted during an outage are not replayed, and no later frame corrects a failed board load. `refresh()` sets `boardLoadError` and rethrows, and nothing retries it. I added `refreshBoardOnOpen()`. It retries with `sseReconnectDelay`, the same jitter as the stream, and a stream error cancels the pending retry, because the next open refreshes again anyway. Retry is the right shape here: a `hello` refresh would not help, since a healthy stream with a timed-out refresh emits no `hello` at all.

The stuck banner has the same root. A timed-out refresh raises the offline banner through `repoos:api-timeout`. Only an open or a frame clears it, so an idle page with a working board kept a false "offline" banner. A board that loads now calls `clearOfflineOnStreamBack()`. I kept that helper's name even though it is now also called from the refresh path, and I left a comment explaining why.

For the copy, the pill now reads "reconnecting", with matching `aria-label` and `title`. The existing `conn-indicator` test asserts the old copy, so I updated it.

The phone case came from the browser run, not from reading code. Below 720 px `.conn-text` was hidden and the dot inherited the header colour, so at 375 px the state was not visible as words. I restored the text with the red tint and pinned the pill with `flex-shrink: 0`.

The browser test drives the built UI with a fixture server. It closes the listener and the streams, changes a count while the server is down, and restarts the server on the same port. The first board request after the restart is refused with 503, which is what a booting server does. That refusal makes the test a real regression check for the retry. It also checks that the pill reads "reconnecting" inside the viewport, that the count reaches 3 without a reload, and that the pill clears.

I committed no code. The QA note is `docs/qa/2026-11-live-reconnect-qa.md`, with screenshots beside it.

## Approaches tried

I first wrote a browser test with no refusal on the first reconnect board request. It passed on the original code, so it did not catch the bug. I then added the refusal. It fails on the original bundle at all three widths and passes on the fix.

My first jsdom tests failed for the wrong reason. The first `onopen` falls inside the store's 2 s init-reuse window, so it correctly skips the refresh. I advanced the fake clock past the window before simulating a reconnect.

I considered a `hello`-triggered refresh and a watchdog for silent connections. Rejected: `hello` cannot cover a timed-out refresh on a healthy stream, and a watchdog needs frames the server does not send. The server's 25 s ping is a comment, which `EventSource` does not expose.

For the phone pill, I first tried removing the text-hiding rule. The header then squeezed the project chip to a sliver. I kept the fix and documented that squeeze as a residual instead of redesigning the header in this pass.

## Challenges and blockers

The biggest trap was the bundle. The browser test loads `dist/ui`, not `src`, so my first "original code" run actually tested my fixed bundle and passed. I found it only after the trace showed a second board request, which turned out to be my own retry. The fix was to rebuild `dist/ui` from the original store, run the browser test, then rebuild from the fix. The QA note states this.

Vitest runs under Node, so the fixture server uses `node:http`, not `Bun.serve`. The first browser run failed in a way that cascaded: a failed assertion left the fixture server stopped, and every later width then failed on connect. The test now restores the server in `finally`.

I could not verify a real `repoos serve` restart, a laptop sleep, or a half-open connection here. Those need a human on their own machine, and the QA note lists them as residuals. The Work board was not checked in the browser at all.

## Key learnings

Failures that no later event corrects need their own retry. "The next frame will fix it" is only true on a busy repo.

A test that passes on the original code proves nothing about the fix. I checked each new browser and jsdom test against the original store. Only the cancel-retry test passes there, because nothing retries yet, and its comment says so.

Browser tests that load a built bundle need a rebuild before each comparison. Without one, the test quietly measures the wrong code.

The phone pill shows that a visible state can still be unreadable. Hiding the text and keeping only a dot in the inherited colour is not a "plain-English state" on a phone, and only a screenshot at the real width showed it.
